components.reason: Replaces the Micro-B J1 with a 16-pin USB 2.0-only USB-C receptacle (VBUS x2, GND x2, D+/D- pairs, CC1, CC2, SBU1/2, shield). 16P is the smallest variant that still exposes CC1 and CC2 separately, which is mandatory for the 5.1 kOhm Rd sink advertisement (IF-001); USB 2.0-only variant avoids unused SS pairs and keeps routing simple on two layers. Through-hole shield tabs give mechanical retention for a repeatedly mated programming port. Horizontal top-mount lets the receptacle sit on the board edge opposite the ESP32 antenna keep-out.
verified_constraints: IF-001: separate CC1/CC2 pins available for independent 5.1 kOhm Rd terminations (UFP sink)
PWR-001: VBUS rated well above USB 2.0 default 5 V / 500 mA sink load
PWR-003: connector current rating (3 A per power contact) exceeds the 500 mA budget
MFG-001: SMD signal pins on 0.5 mm pitch plus plated through-hole shield legs; no blind/buried vias required
USB 2.0-only pinout keeps D+/D- pair short and matched to the bridge

components.reason: Resettable PPTC in series with VBUS for the input_power_protection block. 750 mA hold current is chosen above the 500 mA design load (PWR-003) so the fuse does not trip during ESP32 Wi-Fi TX peaks, while still limiting fault current from the host below typical USB port protection limits. Self-resetting avoids field-servicing a fuse on a USB-powered board.
verified_constraints: PWR-003: hold current 0.75 A > 0.5 A continuous requirement, so no nuisance trip at full load
PWR-001: rated voltage 6 V covers the 5 V VBUS rail
MFG-001: standard 1206 SMD chip, two-layer compatible

Very low line capacitance keeps USB 2.0 full-speed eye compliance intact while giving IEC 61000-4-2 level protection at the connector, the mandatory practice for an exposed user-accessible port. Placed at the connector so surge current returns to the shield/GND without crossing the bridge.

Protects two data lines with one part, keeping the differential pair symmetric and short

components.reason: Fixed 3.3 V linear regulator for the regulator_3v3 block. Rated 1 A output gives 2x margin over the 500 mA requirement, and dropout at 500 mA is far below the 1.7 V available from 5 V VBUS. The decisive factor is thermal: dissipation is (5 V - 3.3 V) x 0.5 A = 0.85 W, which a SOT-223 tab soldered to a copper pour handles with roughly a 50 C rise, whereas SOT-23-5 LDOs (e.g. AP2112K) would exceed their junction limit at this current. Linear rather than switching also avoids switching noise near the ESP32 antenna and needs no inductor on a two-layer board.
verified_constraints: PWR-002: fixed 3.3 V output from 5 V VBUS input
PWR-003: 1 A rated output current covers 500 mA continuous plus ESP32 Wi-Fi TX peaks
PWR-003 thermal: 0.85 W at 500 mA within SOT-223 capability on a copper pour (requires >= 100 mm2 tab pour)
Dropout at 500 mA is below the 1.7 V headroom from 5 V, so regulation holds at minimum USB VBUS (4.75 V)
MFG-001: SOT-223 SMD package, two-layer compatible

components.reason: USB 2.0 full-speed to UART bridge resolving the ESP32-WROOM-32 lack of a native USB peripheral (IF-002). Chosen over CH340 because it needs no external crystal, integrates USB pull-ups and a 3.3 V regulator, has in-box drivers on all major OSes, and the 28-pin variant exposes the full modem-control set so DTR and RTS are available for the auto-program circuit. VIO is tied to the 3.3 V rail so UART, DTR and RTS levels match the ESP32 directly with no level shifter.
verified_constraints: IF-002: USB 2.0 full-speed device with UART plus DTR/RTS modem control for auto-program
IF-002: VIO pin allows 3.3 V I/O referenced to the regulated rail, matching ESP32 logic levels
PWR-003: bus-powered operation draws well under the 500 mA budget
Internal oscillator removes the crystal, saving area toward MECH-001
MFG-001: QFN-28 5x5 mm 0.5 mm pitch with thermal pad, standard two-layer assembly

components.reason: Keeps the specified ESP32-WROOM-32 module family but moves to the current production -32E variant with 4 MB flash. Critically, this symbol exposes the real module pinout including TXD0/RXD0, GPIO0, EN and the full GPIO set, which the placeholder MCU:ESP32-WROOM-32 symbol in the baseline schematic does not; this unblocks the UART programming path (IF-002) and boot strapping (IF-004) that the architecture flagged as an open question. Certified module with integrated PCB antenna avoids RF qualification on a two-layer board.
verified_constraints: IF-002/IF-004: symbol exposes TXD0, RXD0, GPIO0 and EN, so the bridge and reset/boot circuits can be fully connected
IF-003: GPIO21 and GPIO22 available as the default I2C SDA/SCL pair

MECH-003: 18 x 25.5 mm module with integrated antenna at one end, placed at the board edge with an all-layer keep-out
MECH-001: module footprint fits inside the 60 x 45 mm outline

components.reason: The specified digital I2C temperature sensor, in its only production package (SOT-563, 6-lead). Small package supports placing the sensor away from the regulator and module for a representative ambient reading.

components.reason: Two small-signal NPN transistors implementing the standard Espressif/esptool auto-program cross-coupled circuit: DTR and RTS from the CP2102N drive EN and GPIO0 low in the correct sequence so esptool can enter download mode without pressing buttons, and neither line is pulled low when only one of DTR/RTS is asserted. NPN open-collector drive keeps EN and GPIO0 high-impedance in normal operation so the pull-ups dominate.

components.reason: 10 uF X5R bulk capacitors: C1 on protected VBUS at the regulator input, C2 on the 3.3 V regulator output, and C3 as local bulk at the ESP32 3V3 pin to absorb Wi-Fi TX current bursts. 25 V rating on a 5 V/3.3 V application leaves large DC-bias derating margin, so effective capacitance stays near nominal, which matters because the AMS1117 requires real output capacitance for stability.

components.reason: 100 nF X7R high-frequency decoupling, one per supply pin: regulator input, ESP32 3V3, TMP102 VCC, CP2102N VREGIN and CP2102N VIO/VDD. X7R keeps capacitance stable over temperature, and 50 V rating means negligible DC-bias loss. These are the parts that make the TMP102 and bridge supplies quiet enough for reliable I2C and USB operation.
verified_constraints: PWR-002/PWR-004: local decoupling on every power_in pin in the netlist (U1, U2, U3, U4)
